chunks: From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Ja'far, from his fathers (peace be upon them):
That Ali (peace be upon him) did not wash Ammar ibn Yasir, nor Hashim ibn Utbah, and he was the 'Mirqal'; he buried them in their clothes with their blood, and he did not pray over them.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this hadith contains regarding that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did not pray over them is a misconception by the narrator, for we have already clarified the obligation of prayer over the martyrs. It is permissible that the reason for this is that the general public narrate that from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so this [narration] came out in agreement with them.

key_terms.الْمِرْقَالُ: A specific type of burial shroud or garment
key_terms.عَمَّارُ بْنُ يَاسِرٍ: Ammar ibn Yasir, a prominent companion and martyr
key_terms.هَاشِمُ بْنُ عُتْبَةَ: Hashim ibn Utbah, a companion and martyr

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali pray over the martyrs Ammar ibn Yasir and Hashim ibn Utbah?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tahdhib highlights the unique burial practice of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) for Ammar ibn Yasir and Hashim ibn Utbah, who were interred in their garments with their blood, reflecting the urgency of the battlefield context. Shaykh al-Tusi’s student, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, clarifies that this does not negate the general obligation of prayer over martyrs but suggests either a specific circumstantial exception or a deliberate alignment with the Sunni view to maintain unity. This underscores the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling apparent contradictions through contextual nuance rather than literal contradiction.
